To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FOG-1 and FOG-3 are expressed in the mouse ovary and can modulate Müllerian inhibiting substance expression.
FOG-1 and GATA-1 are expressed in the mouse ovary during development and that FOG-4 and GATA-5 are expressed during postnatal development.
FOG- 2 is expressed in the developing ovine ovary and that FOG-1 is expressed in the fetal testes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of FGA-4 and FGA-2 in the developing mouse ovary.

the identification of the transcription factors involved in the regulation of the MIS gene in granulosa and thecal cells and with the identification of factors regulating their expression in ovarian follicular cells during development.
the expression of Gata4 and FOG2 during mouse gonadogenesis and their potential role in ovarian development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FOG-1 and FOG-3 are expressed in the developing ovducts, whereas FOG-2 seems to be expressed in the ovary.
the GATA transcription factor and its coactivator, FOG-1, are essential for the formation of the bipotential gonad.
FOG-1 is expressed only in the testis and that FOG- 2 is expressed only in ovary, and that FOG proteins are essential for GATA- 4-mediated transactivation of MIS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FOG-2 transcriptional repressor has a specific role counteracting the effect of GATAs on MIS gene expression in granulosa and thecal cells.
FOG-1 and FOG-3 are expressed in the testis but are down-regulated in the ovary.
the FOG-2/GATA-4 interaction is essential in maintaining MIS expression and, thus, in the development of the ovary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FOG- 2 is expressed in the developing ovine and that its expression is not lost in the fetal ovine ovary, as has been suggested in the mouse.
the expression pattern of FOG-1 and FOG-1 in the fetal and adult ovary is distinct and may have a role in the regulation of MIS expression.
FOG-1 and GATA-1 are not expressed in the developing ovotestis, whereas FOG-2/GATA-4 is expressed in both ovary and testis.
